rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: A COSHH assessment concentrates on hazards and risks from hazardous substances in the workplace.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: Harmful substances can be created by work processes, including wood dust, silica dust and welding fumes.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: Product labels and safety data sheets should be used to identify harmful substances, with supplier advice sought where needed.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: Risk assessment should consider exposure routes, frequency and duration, and workers, contractors, visitors or members of the public who could be exposed.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: Exposure should first be prevented at source by avoiding, substituting or using a safer process or form where reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: Where exposure cannot be prevented it must be adequately controlled, with control measures working and applicable workplace exposure limits observed.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: Local exhaust ventilation used as a control must be examined and tested at least every 14 months by a competent person.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: Foreseeable hazardous-substance emergencies require suitable equipment, casualty procedures, trained people and arrangements for contaminated waste.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: COSHH risk depends on the exact substance, process, concentration, exposure route, duration, people exposed, control condition and emergency arrangements.

rows.source: HSE COSHH hazardous-substance assessment and control guidance
rows.verified: General COSHH guidance does not prove exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and is not an exact illness probability.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: Employers must prevent or reduce health and safety risks arising from exposure to noise at work.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: Employers must assess the risks to employees from noise at work.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: Employers must take action to reduce noise exposure that produces risk.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: Hearing protection must be provided where exposure cannot be reduced enough by other methods.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: Employers must ensure legal limits on occupational noise exposure are not exceeded.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: Workers must receive suitable information, instruction and training, and health surveillance is required where there is a risk to health.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: The lower and upper daily or weekly exposure action values are 80 dB(A) and 85 dB(A), with peak values of 135 dB(C) and 137 dB(C).

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: The daily or weekly exposure limit value is 87 dB(A) and the peak exposure limit value is 140 dB(C).

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: Noise risk depends on measured daily or weekly exposure, peak sound pressure, task duration, hearing-protection attenuation, worker susceptibility and control performance.

rows.source: HSE Control of Noise at Work guidance
rows.verified: General noise guidance or an area-level noise source does not establish an exact parcel-level hearing-loss probability.
